exposure: Patient-controlled epidural analgesia (PCEA) with 1 mg/mL ropivacaine and 2 μg/mL fentanyl
Continuous epidural infusion (CEI) with 1 mg/mL ropivacaine and 2 μg/mL fentanyl
PCEA with 0.8 mg/mL bupivacaine and 2 μg/mL fentanyl
CEI with 0.8 mg/mL bupivacaine and 2 μg/mL fentanyl
finding: PCEA with 1 mg/mL ropivacaine and 2 μg/mL fentanyl might provide the greatest benefit for labor analgesia, with a lower instrumental delivery rate compared to CEI but a higher rate compared to PCEA with bupivacaine.
mod_finding: The Cesarean section rate was higher in the CEI groups compared to the PCEA groups, while the instrumental delivery rate was lower in the PCEA groups with ropivacaine compared to the other groups.
